title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 Boss Hopes GTA6 Pushes Game Prices Up
description: Warhorse Studios co-founder Martin Klima hopes GTA 6 will usher in a new normal for higher game prices, calling it necessary for industry survival.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 Boss Hopes GTA6 Pushes Game Prices Up

The ongoing debate surrounding the pricing of modern video games has taken a fresh turn. According to a report by gaming media outlet Eurogamer, Martin Klima, co-founder of Warhorse Studios—the development team behind last year's historical RPG *Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2*—has voiced his support for higher game prices, suggesting that *GTA 6* might be the catalyst to usher in a new normal for the industry.

## A Necessary Move for Industry Survival

In recent discussions, Klima made no secret of his stance on the matter, stating that he is crossing his fingers for a shift toward higher price points. In his view, this adjustment is not only "long overdue" but also fundamentally "necessary for this business to survive."

As development budgets, team sizes, and production values for AAA titles continue to soar to unprecedented heights, studios face mounting financial pressures. While development costs have expanded exponentially over the years, baseline game prices have largely lagged behind, creating a growing gap between financial input and output for many developers across the sector.

## Could GTA6 Set a New Standard?

When looking at who might reshape consumer expectations and industry standards, Klima pointed to *GTA 6* as the potential title to lead the charge. Given the colossal scale, immense anticipation, and unprecedented market reach of Rockstar Games' upcoming blockbuster, any pricing decision it makes tends to send shockwaves throughout the entire gaming ecosystem.

Industry observers note that flagship releases of this magnitude often act as pioneers, paving the way for wider market acceptance when it comes to structural shifts in product pricing.

## Editor's Take

Martin Klima's comments highlight the silent financial strain burdening developers in an era of skyrocketing production costs. While higher price tags are never an easy pill for players to swallow, the broader question remains whether the industry's economic model can sustain itself without adjustments. All eyes are on how upcoming giants like *GTA 6* will handle the pricing conversation.
